details.label: Discussion
details.text: Scattered thunderstorms are in the process of developing within parts of the Mid-South into the Southeast. The highest coverage of storms will likely occur ahead of a weak perturbation in southern Arkansas and where temperatures have reached the upper 90s F. Rich surface moisture/large PWAT values and steeper than typical mid-level lapse rates will support a threat for damaging downburst winds and perhaps isolated large hail. A greater localized wind threat may emerge as storm outflows congeal amid a weakly sheared environment. Cooler air is evident farther east where outflow continues to modify. Storm coverage there is less certain. A watch is possible for portions of these regions depending on convective trends the remainder of this afternoon

details.label: Summary
details.text: An organizing cluster of storms will pose increasing potential to produce damaging wind gusts and a couple of tornadoes into and across the Greater Philadelphia vicinity through the the 6-7 PM EDT time frame

details.label: Discussion
details.text: A more prominent, but still compact, clustering of intensifying thunderstorm development is ongoing south/southeast of Harrisburg PA. This does appear focused near a weak developing frontal wave, and is perhaps being supported by forcing for ascent downstream of an east-northeastward propagating 50+ kt mid-level jet streak, based on the latest Rapid Refresh output. Strongest recent boundary-layer destabilization, associated with insolation and thermal/moisture advection, has become focused to the north of the Greater Baltimore area the past few hours. Updraft inflow emanating from this environment, probably will support further upscale growth and intensification of the convective system into and across the Greater Philadelphia area through 22-23Z. This may include evolving supercell structures posing a risk for tornadoes, and increasing risk for strong to severe surface gusts

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Weak thunderstorms have recently initiated within Cherry County, NE this afternoon along a weak surface trough. Moisture return continues into the central Plains along the western flank of a surface high. Dewpoints have generally held in the low/mid 60s F despite the strong heating/mixing. Given the mid-level height rises that are occurring, storm coverage/longevity is in question. With around 40 kt of effective shear and modestly steep mid-level lapse rates on the 18Z LBF sounding, mature/sustained storms would likely be supercellular and capable of large hail (up to around 2 in.) and severe wind gusts. It is not clear whether a watch will be needed this afternoon given potentially isolated coverage. However, convective trends will continue to be monitored
